starting_point: Interest in risk, documentation and how information is used. Compliance, operations or audit experience can support governance work; technical security work needs additional IT foundations.
mapping_note: Cyber Security topics support this introductory path. The data/AI governance exercises are workshop additions, not a dedicated roadmap.sh data-governance curriculum.

phase_1.label: Describe the information and its owners
phase_1.slide: A data inventory, flow diagram and access matrix
actions: Use the fictional FAQ assistant from the workshop. List its data sources, owners, purposes, users and retention assumptions.
Learn basic authentication, authorisation and risk terminology. Separate user-provided instructions from trusted system rules.
phase_1.output: A data inventory, simple flow diagram and role/access matrix.

phase_2.label: Choose proportionate controls
phase_2.slide: Risks linked to owners, controls and tests
actions: Write five realistic risks, including unauthorised access, disclosure and unsupported AI answers.
Design controls and test scenarios. Practise only on your own local demo or an explicitly authorised training environment.
phase_2.output: A risk register, control checklist and five test scenarios.

phase_3.label: Test and record the decisions
phase_3.slide: Evidence from a review and an incident exercise
actions: Run the test scenarios and document failures, remediation and remaining risks.
Rehearse a fictional disclosure incident and produce a concise review recommendation with named accountable roles.
phase_3.output: A sample assurance pack with evidence and a short incident playbook.

portfolio: A governance and security review of a fictional internal FAQ assistant.
tools: A document editor, spreadsheet and optional local demo application. No offensive tooling or paid certification is required.
acceptance: Every listed dataset has an owner, purpose, access rule and retention assumption.
Five risks each link to a control, accountable role and documented verification result.
The final recommendation distinguishes verified controls, open issues and assumptions requiring specialist review.
first_step: Draw where information enters, where it is stored and who can see the output.
beginner_adjustment: Choose either governance analysis or technical security as the main direction after the introductory month. Neither can be mastered as a single combined 90-day path.
